result.topic_en: Draft passage on Riemann surfaces T: how branch points (Windungspunkte) of various orders arise, when the surface is completely determined, the notion of a continuous function on T, and §6, an integral theorem relating a surface integral of derivatives of X, Y over T to a boundary integral (Green/Stokes type).

items.english: Evidently the surface T is completely determined if and only if, besides the position of its boundary, it is also specified where and in which parts of the surface branch points occur.

items.quote: Zunächst[?] aber noch einige allgemeine Sätze.
items.english: But first some more general theorems.

items.quote:
Sind X u. Y zwei in allen Punkten von T stetige Functionen, so ist das
über alle Elemente dT dieser Fläche ausgedehnte Integral
$\int\left(\frac{\partial X}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial Y}{\partial x}\right)dT=\int(Y\cos\xi - X\cos\eta)\,ds$
items.english: If X and Y are two functions continuous at all points of T, then the integral over all elements dT of this surface equals the boundary integral of (Y cos ξ − X cos η) ds.
